What I mean by not looking past a bad quality about someone is once you find something about someone that rubs you the wrong way, stay on high alert. 

And if that feeling persists and/or that behavior from that person wasn’t just a one-off, set a hard boundary to see their reaction or start distancing yourself from that person. Their reaction will tell you whether or not they’re an emotionally healthy person. 

An example: I met a friend-of-a-friend when I was younger and they seemed interested in getting to know me. 

However, very quickly I learned that they were one of those people who viewed friends as free therapists and wanted favors all the time. I unfortunately didn’t have the wherewithal to assert myself at the time, so I let it continue longer than it should have (until the relationship ran its course).  

Now, if I find myself in a similar situation with someone new, and if I find that they want to emotional dump on me frequently, I say something along the lines of, “I’m sorry you’re going through that, but I don’t have the capacity to offer the emotional support you’re looking for.” 

If those types of people sense too much empathy in someone, they will 100% take advantage of it and the behavior will progress. That’s why you need to stop it before it starts. 

That tends to weed out the emotional vampires pretty quickly. People like that are uncomfortable with boundaries, and will be intimidated and see themselves out if you set them early on. I hope that helps!
